sets.name: Newton's laws of motion
sets.summary: The foundation of classical mechanics, from the Principia.

items.name: First law
items.text: A body stays at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by a net force.

items.name: Second law
items.text: Net force equals the rate of change of momentum.

items.name: Third law
items.text: Forces come in equal and opposite pairs.

items.name: Universal gravitation
items.text: Every mass attracts every other with a force proportional to their masses and inversely to distance squared.

sets.name: Laws of thermodynamics
sets.summary: Four laws governing heat, energy and entropy.

items.name: Zeroth law
items.text: Two systems each in equilibrium with a third are in equilibrium with each other.

items.name: First law
items.text: Energy is conserved: internal energy changes by heat added minus work done.

items.name: Second law
items.text: Entropy of an isolated system never decreases; heat flows spontaneously from hot to cold.

items.name: Third law
items.text: Entropy approaches a minimum as temperature approaches absolute zero, which cannot be reached in finitely many steps.

sets.name: Maxwell's equations
sets.summary: Four equations that unify electricity, magnetism and light.

items.name: Gauss's law
items.text: Electric charge is the source of electric field.

items.name: Gauss's law for magnetism
items.text: There are no magnetic monopoles.

items.name: Faraday's law
items.text: A changing magnetic field induces an electric field.

items.name: Ampère–Maxwell law
items.text: Currents and changing electric fields produce magnetic fields.

sets.name: Postulates of special relativity
sets.summary: Two postulates from which time dilation, length contraction and E = mc² follow.

items.name: Principle of relativity
items.text: The laws of physics are the same in every inertial frame.

items.name: Constancy of light speed
items.text: Light in vacuum moves at c for every inertial observer, whatever the motion of the source.

sets.name: Principles of general relativity
sets.summary: Gravity as the curvature of spacetime.

items.name: Equivalence principle
items.text: Locally, a gravitational field is indistinguishable from acceleration.

items.name: General covariance
items.text: Physical laws take the same form in all coordinate systems.

items.name: Geodesic motion
items.text: Free bodies follow geodesics: the straightest possible paths in curved spacetime.

items.name: Field equations
items.text: Matter and energy determine curvature.

sets.name: Postulates of quantum mechanics
sets.summary: The standard textbook axioms of quantum theory.

items.name: State
items.text: A system's state is a unit vector in a complex Hilbert space.
items.mathml: <math><mrow><mi>|</mi><mi>ψ</mi><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">⟩</mo><mo separator="true">,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>ψ</mi><mi>|</mi><mi>ψ</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>

items.name: Observables
items.text: Measurable quantities are self-adjoint operators.

items.name: Measurement outcomes
items.text: A measurement yields an eigenvalue of the observable.

items.name: Born rule
items.text: The probability of outcome a is the squared overlap with its eigenstate.

items.name: Collapse
items.text: After measurement the state becomes the corresponding eigenstate.

items.name: Time evolution
items.text: Between measurements the state evolves by the Schrödinger equation.

items.name: Symmetrization
items.text: Identical bosons have symmetric states; identical fermions antisymmetric.

sets.name: Conservation laws
sets.summary: Quantities that stay constant in isolated systems, each tied to a symmetry.

items.name: Energy
items.text: Conserved; follows from time-translation symmetry.

items.name: Linear momentum
items.text: Conserved; follows from space-translation symmetry.

items.name: Angular momentum
items.text: Conserved; follows from rotational symmetry.

items.name: Electric charge
items.text: Conserved; follows from gauge symmetry.

items.name: Baryon and lepton number
items.text: Conserved in all observed processes (approximate in theory).

sets.name: Dalton's atomic theory
sets.summary: The first modern atomic theory, later refined (isotopes, subatomic particles).

items.name: Atoms
items.text: Matter is made of indivisible atoms.

items.name: Identity
items.text: Atoms of one element are identical in mass and properties.

items.name: Combination
items.text: Compounds form from atoms in simple whole-number ratios.

items.name: Rearrangement
items.text: Reactions rearrange atoms; atoms are not created or destroyed.

sets.name: Periodic law
sets.summary: Element properties repeat periodically, by atomic number.

items.name: Periodicity
items.text: Properties of elements are periodic functions of atomic number.

items.name: Prediction
items.text: Gaps in the table correspond to undiscovered elements (gallium, scandium, germanium were predicted).

sets.name: Principles of chemical bonding
sets.summary: How atoms share and transfer electrons.

items.name: Octet rule
items.text: Main-group atoms tend toward eight valence electrons.

items.name: Electronegativity
items.text: Atoms differ in how strongly they pull shared electrons.

items.name: VSEPR
items.text: Electron pairs around an atom spread apart to minimize repulsion, setting molecular shape.

items.name: Aufbau, Hund and Pauli
items.text: Electrons fill the lowest orbitals first, spread out before pairing, and no two share all quantum numbers.

sets.name: Cell theory
sets.summary: The basic unit of life.

items.name: All living things are cells
items.text: Every organism is made of one or more cells.

items.name: Basic unit
items.text: The cell is the basic unit of structure and function.

items.name: Cells from cells
items.text: All cells arise from pre-existing cells (omnis cellula e cellula).

sets.name: Darwinian natural selection
sets.summary: The mechanism of adaptive evolution.

items.name: Variation
items.text: Individuals in a population differ.

items.name: Inheritance
items.text: Many differences are passed to offspring.

items.name: Overproduction
items.text: More offspring are born than can survive.

items.name: Differential survival
items.text: Individuals with helpful variations survive and reproduce more.

items.name: Accumulation
items.text: Over generations, helpful traits become common and populations change.

sets.name: Mendel's laws of inheritance
sets.summary: Rediscovered in 1900; the start of genetics.

items.name: Segregation
items.text: Each parent passes one of its two alleles for a gene, at random.

items.name: Independent assortment
items.text: Genes for different traits are inherited independently (unless linked).

items.name: Dominance
items.text: One allele can mask the effect of another.

sets.name: Central dogma of molecular biology
sets.summary: How genetic information flows.

items.name: Replication
items.text: DNA makes DNA.

items.name: Transcription
items.text: DNA makes RNA.

items.name: Translation
items.text: RNA makes protein.

items.name: No reverse flow from protein
items.text: Sequence information cannot pass from protein back to nucleic acid (reverse transcription RNA→DNA does occur).

sets.name: Germ theory of disease
sets.summary: Many diseases are caused by microorganisms.

items.name: Koch 1
items.text: The microbe is found in every case of the disease.

items.name: Koch 2
items.text: It can be isolated and grown in pure culture.

items.name: Koch 3
items.text: The cultured microbe causes the disease in a healthy host.

items.name: Koch 4
items.text: The same microbe is recovered from that host.

sets.name: Modern evolutionary synthesis
sets.summary: Darwin combined with Mendelian genetics.

items.name: Genetic basis
items.text: Variation comes from mutation and recombination.

items.name: Mechanisms
items.text: Evolution acts by selection, drift, mutation and gene flow.

items.name: Gradualism
items.text: Small genetic changes accumulate into large differences.

items.name: Speciation
items.text: New species arise when populations become reproductively isolated.

sets.name: Principles of ecology
sets.summary: How organisms and environments interact.

items.name: Competitive exclusion
items.text: Two species competing for one limiting resource can't coexist indefinitely.

items.name: Energy flow
items.text: Energy flows one way through food chains and is lost as heat at each step.

items.name: Nutrient cycling
items.text: Matter cycles through ecosystems.

items.name: Carrying capacity
items.text: Environments support a limited population.

sets.name: Plate tectonics
sets.summary: Earth's surface is broken into moving plates.

items.name: Lithospheric plates
items.text: The rigid outer shell is divided into plates riding on the softer asthenosphere.

items.name: Divergence
items.text: Plates separate at mid-ocean ridges, making new crust (sea-floor spreading).

items.name: Convergence
items.text: Plates collide, building mountains or sinking at subduction zones.

items.name: Transform boundaries
items.text: Plates slide past each other, causing earthquakes.

sets.name: Steno's principles of stratigraphy
sets.summary: Reading time from rock layers.

items.name: Superposition
items.text: Lower layers are older.

items.name: Original horizontality
items.text: Layers are deposited flat.

items.name: Lateral continuity
items.text: Layers extend sideways until they thin out.

items.name: Cross-cutting relationships
items.text: Anything cutting a layer is younger than it.

sets.name: Cosmological principle and Big Bang model
sets.summary: The standard framework of cosmology.

items.name: Cosmological principle
items.text: On large scales the universe is the same everywhere and in every direction.

items.name: Expansion
items.text: Space itself is expanding.

items.name: Hot dense origin
items.text: The universe evolved from an extremely hot, dense early state about 13.8 billion years ago.

items.name: Relic radiation
items.text: The cooled afterglow remains as the cosmic microwave background (≈2.725 K).

sets.name: Principles of the scientific method
sets.summary: The working rules of empirical inquiry.

items.name: Empiricism
items.text: Claims must answer to observation and experiment.

items.name: Falsifiability
items.text: A scientific claim must risk being shown false (Popper, 1934).

items.name: Reproducibility
items.text: Results must hold up when others repeat the work.

items.name: Parsimony
items.text: Prefer the simplest explanation that fits the evidence (Occam's razor).

items.name: Provisional knowledge
items.text: Theories are accepted tentatively and revised with new evidence.

sets.name: Standard Model of particle physics
sets.summary: The theory of all known particles and three of the four forces.

items.name: Gauge symmetry
items.text: Forces arise from the gauge group SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1).
items.mathml: <math><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>U</mi><msub><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>C</mi></msub><mo>×</mo><mi>S</mi><mi>U</mi><msub><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>×</mo><mi>U</mi><msub><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>Y</mi></msub></mrow></math>

items.name: Matter
items.text: Six quarks and six leptons in three generations.

items.name: Force carriers
items.text: Gluons, W and Z bosons, and photons carry the strong, weak and electromagnetic forces.

items.name: Higgs mechanism
items.text: The Higgs field gives mass to the W, Z and fermions (Higgs boson found 2012).

theories.name: Heliocentrism
theories.claim: The Earth and planets orbit the Sun.
theories.evidence: Simpler planetary motions; Galileo's phases of Venus (1610); stellar parallax (1838).

theories.name: Kepler's laws of planetary motion
theories.claim: Planets move on ellipses with predictable speeds and periods.
theories.evidence: Tycho Brahe's precise observations of Mars.

theories.name: Galilean moons
theories.claim: Jupiter has moons orbiting it.
theories.evidence: Telescope observations; not everything orbits the Earth.

theories.name: Universal gravitation
theories.claim: One force explains falling apples and orbiting planets.
theories.evidence: Derived Kepler's laws; predicted Halley's comet's return (1758).

theories.name: Circulation of the blood
theories.claim: The heart pumps blood around a closed circuit.
theories.evidence: Measured volumes pumped; one-way valves in veins.

theories.name: Microorganisms
theories.claim: Tiny living things exist everywhere.

theories.name: Cells
theories.claim: Living tissue is made of small compartments.
theories.evidence: Cork under a microscope in Micrographia.

theories.name: Wave theory of light
theories.claim: Light is a wave.

theories.name: Composition of white light
theories.claim: White light is a mix of colours.
theories.evidence: Prism experiments splitting and recombining light.

theories.name: Oxygen and combustion
theories.claim: Burning is combination with oxygen, not loss of phlogiston.
theories.evidence: Careful weighing showed metals gain mass when burned.

theories.name: Conservation of mass
theories.claim: Mass is conserved in chemical reactions.

theories.name: Atomic theory
theories.claim: Matter is made of atoms combining in fixed ratios.
theories.evidence: Laws of definite and multiple proportions.

theories.name: Avogadro's hypothesis
theories.claim: Equal gas volumes hold equal numbers of molecules.
theories.evidence: Gay-Lussac's combining volumes; accepted after Cannizzaro (1860).

theories.name: Vaccination
theories.claim: Exposure to cowpox protects against smallpox.
theories.evidence: Inoculated James Phipps, who resisted smallpox.

theories.name: Deep time and uniformitarianism
theories.claim: Earth is very old and shaped by slow, ongoing processes.

theories.name: Extinction
theories.claim: Species can disappear entirely.
theories.evidence: Mammoth and mastodon fossils unlike living elephants.

theories.name: Electromagnetism
theories.claim: Electric currents create magnetic fields.
theories.evidence: A current deflected a compass needle.

theories.name: Electromagnetic induction
theories.claim: Changing magnetism produces electricity.
theories.evidence: Moving a magnet through a coil made a current; led to generators.

theories.name: Conservation of energy
theories.claim: Energy changes form but is never lost.
theories.evidence: Joule's paddle-wheel measured the mechanical equivalent of heat.

theories.name: Second law of thermodynamics
theories.claim: Entropy increases; heat engines can't be perfectly efficient.

theories.name: Cell theory
theories.claim: All living things are made of cells, which come from cells.
theories.evidence: Microscopy of plant and animal tissue.

theories.name: Evolution by natural selection
theories.claim: Species change over generations through differential survival.
theories.evidence: Fossils, biogeography, artificial selection, homology; later genetics.

theories.name: Germ theory
theories.claim: Microbes cause infection and decay.
theories.evidence: Swan-neck flask experiment; Koch identified anthrax, TB, cholera bacteria.

theories.name: Antiseptic surgery
theories.claim: Killing germs in wounds prevents infection.
theories.evidence: Carbolic acid sharply cut surgical deaths.

theories.name: Handwashing and childbed fever
theories.claim: Doctors' unwashed hands spread puerperal fever.
theories.evidence: Chlorine handwashing dropped maternal mortality dramatically.

theories.name: Epidemiology of cholera
theories.claim: Cholera spreads through contaminated water.
theories.evidence: Mapped cases around the Broad Street pump.

theories.name: Mendelian inheritance
theories.claim: Traits pass in discrete units in predictable ratios.

theories.name: Periodic table
theories.claim: Elements fall into periodic families.
theories.evidence: Predicted gallium, scandium and germanium before discovery.

theories.name: Electromagnetic theory of light
theories.claim: Light is an electromagnetic wave.
theories.evidence: Calculated wave speed matched light; Hertz made radio waves (1887).

theories.name: Structural chemistry (benzene)
theories.claim: Carbon forms chains and rings; benzene is a ring.

theories.name: Kinetic theory of gases
theories.claim: Gas behaviour comes from moving molecules.

theories.name: Electrons
theories.claim: Atoms contain small negative particles.

theories.name: X-rays
theories.claim: A penetrating new radiation exists.
theories.evidence: Photographed the bones of a hand.

theories.name: Radioactivity
theories.who: Henri Becquerel; Marie and Pierre Curie
theories.claim: Some atoms emit radiation spontaneously.
theories.evidence: Uranium fogged photographic plates; discovery of polonium and radium.

theories.name: Quantum hypothesis
theories.claim: Energy is exchanged in discrete quanta.

theories.name: Light quanta (photons)
theories.claim: Light comes in particles of energy hf.
theories.evidence: Explained the photoelectric effect; confirmed by Millikan (1916).

theories.name: Brownian motion explained
theories.claim: Jittering particles are pushed by molecules.

theories.name: Special relativity
theories.claim: Space and time depend on motion; light speed is constant.

theories.name: Atomic nucleus
theories.claim: An atom's mass and positive charge sit in a tiny nucleus.

theories.name: Bohr model
theories.claim: Electrons occupy discrete orbits.

theories.name: Continental drift
theories.claim: Continents have moved over time.
theories.evidence: Matching coastlines, fossils and rocks; accepted after plate tectonics.

theories.name: Chromosome theory of inheritance
theories.claim: Genes lie on chromosomes.

theories.name: General relativity
theories.claim: Gravity is curved spacetime.

theories.name: Expanding universe
theories.claim: Galaxies are moving apart.

theories.name: Other galaxies
theories.claim: The Milky Way is one of many galaxies.

theories.name: Quantum mechanics
theories.claim: Matter and light obey probabilistic wave mechanics.

theories.name: Uncertainty principle
theories.claim: Some pairs of quantities can't both be precise.
theories.evidence: Follows from wave mechanics; confirmed in every test.

theories.name: Antimatter
theories.claim: Every particle has an antiparticle.
theories.evidence: Positron tracks in a cloud chamber.

theories.name: Neutron
theories.claim: The nucleus contains neutral particles.
theories.evidence: Beryllium radiation knocking protons from paraffin.

theories.name: Penicillin
theories.claim: A mould kills bacteria.
theories.evidence: Contaminated culture plate; mass production in WWII.

theories.name: Nuclear fission
theories.claim: Heavy nuclei can split, releasing energy.
theories.evidence: Barium found after bombarding uranium with neutrons.

theories.name: Stellar nucleosynthesis
theories.who: Hans Bethe; Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler, Hoyle
theories.claim: Stars fuse light elements into heavier ones.

theories.name: Dark matter
theories.claim: Galaxies contain much more mass than we see.
theories.evidence: Flat galaxy rotation curves; gravitational lensing.

theories.name: DNA as genetic material
theories.claim: Genes are made of DNA.

theories.name: DNA double helix
theories.claim: DNA is two complementary strands in a helix.

theories.name: Semiconservative replication
theories.claim: Each new DNA keeps one old strand.

theories.name: Genetic code
theories.claim: Three-letter codons specify amino acids.
theories.evidence: Synthetic RNA translated in cell-free systems.

theories.name: Operon model
theories.claim: Genes are switched on and off by regulators.
theories.evidence: The lac operon in E. coli.

theories.name: Endosymbiotic theory
theories.claim: Mitochondria and chloroplasts were once free-living bacteria.
theories.evidence: Their own DNA and double membranes.

theories.name: Plate tectonics
theories.claim: Earth's crust moves in plates.
theories.evidence: Magnetic stripes on the sea floor; earthquake belts.

theories.name: Big Bang
theories.claim: The universe began hot and dense and has expanded.

theories.name: Cosmic microwave background
theories.claim: The sky glows with relic radiation.
theories.evidence: Persistent microwave noise from every direction.

theories.name: Quarks
theories.claim: Protons and neutrons are made of quarks.

theories.name: Electroweak unification
theories.claim: Electromagnetism and the weak force are one.
theories.evidence: Neutral currents (1973); W and Z bosons (1983).

theories.name: Quantum chromodynamics
theories.claim: Gluons bind quarks with a force that weakens at short range.

theories.name: Higgs boson
theories.claim: A field gives particles mass.
theories.evidence: 125 GeV particle found at the LHC.

theories.name: Pulsars
theories.claim: Rapidly spinning neutron stars emit beams.

theories.name: Black holes observed
theories.claim: Collapsed objects with event horizons exist.
theories.evidence: Cygnus X-1; Event Horizon Telescope image (2019).

theories.name: Exoplanets
theories.claim: Planets orbit other Sun-like stars.

theories.name: Accelerating expansion
theories.claim: The expansion of the universe is speeding up.
theories.evidence: Distant type Ia supernovae fainter than expected.

theories.name: Gravitational waves
theories.claim: Spacetime ripples travel at light speed.
theories.evidence: Merger of two black holes detected.

theories.name: Neutrino oscillation
theories.claim: Neutrinos change type, so they have mass.

theories.name: Ozone depletion by CFCs
theories.claim: CFCs destroy stratospheric ozone.

theories.name: Greenhouse effect
theories.claim: CO₂ and water vapour trap heat.

theories.name: Anthropogenic climate change
theories.claim: Human emissions are warming the climate.
theories.evidence: Temperature records, ice cores, isotope fingerprints.

theories.name: Asteroid impact extinction
theories.claim: An impact ended the dinosaurs' era.

theories.name: Prions
theories.claim: Misfolded proteins can be infectious.

theories.name: H. pylori and ulcers
theories.claim: Most stomach ulcers are caused by bacteria.
theories.evidence: Marshall drank a culture and developed gastritis.

theories.name: Reverse transcriptase
theories.claim: RNA can be copied into DNA.

theories.name: Polymerase chain reaction
theories.claim: DNA can be copied exponentially in a test tube.
theories.evidence: Thermal cycling with a heat-stable polymerase.

theories.name: Human Genome Project
theories.claim: The human genome sequence is mapped.
theories.evidence: About 3 billion base pairs; about 20,000 protein-coding genes.

theories.name: CRISPR gene editing
theories.claim: A bacterial immune system can cut DNA at chosen sites.

theories.name: Induced pluripotent stem cells
theories.claim: Adult cells can be reprogrammed into stem cells.
theories.evidence: Four transcription factors reset mouse cells.

theories.name: Archaea as a domain
theories.claim: Life has three domains, not two.

theories.name: Neuron doctrine
theories.claim: The nervous system is made of separate cells.

theories.name: Action potential
theories.claim: Nerve signals are ion currents through voltage-gated channels.

theories.name: Chemical neurotransmission
theories.claim: Nerves signal with chemicals.
theories.evidence: Vagus-nerve fluid slowed a second frog heart.

theories.name: Insulin
theories.claim: A pancreatic hormone controls blood sugar.
theories.evidence: Pancreatic extract kept diabetic dogs alive.

theories.name: Vitamins
theories.claim: Trace nutrients prevent deficiency diseases.

theories.name: Scurvy and citrus
theories.claim: Citrus prevents scurvy.
theories.evidence: One of the first controlled clinical trials.

theories.name: Blood groups
theories.claim: Blood comes in compatible types.

theories.name: Immune clonal selection
theories.claim: Each lymphocyte makes one antibody and multiplies on contact with its antigen.

theories.name: Photosynthesis
theories.claim: Plants use light to make sugar and release oxygen.
theories.evidence: Ingenhousz's light experiments; Calvin's carbon-14 tracing (1950s).

theories.name: Krebs cycle
theories.claim: A cycle of reactions oxidizes food to make energy carriers.

theories.name: Chemiosmosis
theories.claim: ATP is made using a proton gradient.

theories.name: Hydrogen bonding and protein structure
theories.claim: Proteins fold into α-helices and β-sheets.
theories.evidence: Model building from bond geometry; X-ray data.

theories.name: Chemical bond (quantum)
theories.claim: Covalent bonds come from shared electron waves.

theories.name: Chemical equilibrium
theories.claim: Reactions reach balance governed by mass action.

theories.name: Electrolytic dissociation
theories.claim: Salts split into ions in water.

theories.name: Catalysis
theories.claim: Some substances speed reactions without being used up.

theories.name: Isotopes
theories.claim: Atoms of one element can differ in mass.

theories.name: Synthesis of urea
theories.claim: Organic compounds can be made from inorganic ones.

theories.name: Polymer theory
theories.claim: Plastics and rubber are giant chain molecules.

theories.name: Fullerenes
theories.claim: Carbon forms closed cages like C₆₀.

theories.name: Graphene
theories.claim: Single-atom carbon sheets are stable.

theories.name: Superconductivity
theories.claim: Some metals lose all resistance when cold.

theories.name: BCS theory
theories.claim: Electron pairs carry current without resistance.
theories.evidence: Explained the energy gap and isotope effect.

theories.name: Transistor
theories.claim: Semiconductors can amplify and switch signals.

theories.name: Laser
theories.claim: Stimulated emission produces coherent light.

theories.name: Bose–Einstein condensate
theories.claim: Cold bosons collapse into one quantum state.

theories.name: Quantum entanglement tests
theories.claim: Nature violates Bell inequalities.

theories.name: Chaos theory
theories.claim: Deterministic systems can be unpredictable.

theories.name: Information theory
theories.claim: Information can be measured in bits.

theories.name: Theory of computation
theories.claim: A simple machine can compute anything computable.
theories.evidence: Turing machine model; equivalence with lambda calculus.

theories.name: Cognitive dissonance
theories.claim: People feel discomfort from conflicting beliefs and act to reduce it.

theories.name: Classical conditioning
theories.claim: Neutral cues can come to trigger reflexes.

theories.name: Operant conditioning
theories.claim: Behaviour is shaped by its consequences.

theories.name: Cognitive development stages
theories.claim: Children's thinking develops in stages.

theories.name: Attachment theory
theories.claim: Early bonds with caregivers shape development.

theories.name: Prospect theory
theories.claim: People weigh losses more than equal gains.

theories.name: Supply and demand
theories.claim: Prices settle where supply meets demand.

theories.name: Comparative advantage
theories.claim: Trade benefits both sides even if one is better at everything.

theories.name: Keynesian economics
theories.claim: Total demand drives output and employment in the short run.

theories.name: Game theory
theories.claim: Strategic decisions can be analysed mathematically.

theories.name: Island biogeography
theories.claim: Island species counts balance immigration and extinction.
theories.evidence: Defaunation experiments in the Florida Keys.

theories.name: Punctuated equilibrium
theories.claim: Species often stay stable then change quickly.

theories.name: Kin selection
theories.claim: Helping relatives can spread genes.

theories.name: Neutral theory of evolution
theories.claim: Most molecular changes are neutral and spread by drift.

theories.name: Gaia hypothesis
theories.claim: Life and Earth form a self-regulating system.

theories.name: Milankovitch cycles
theories.claim: Orbital wobbles pace the ice ages.

theories.name: Sea-floor spreading
theories.claim: New ocean crust forms at mid-ocean ridges.

theories.name: Earth's core
theories.claim: Earth has a liquid outer core and solid inner core.

theories.name: Mohorovičić discontinuity
theories.claim: A boundary separates crust from mantle.
theories.evidence: Sudden change in seismic wave speed.

theories.name: Age of the Earth
theories.claim: Earth is about 4.55 billion years old.

theories.name: Big Bang nucleosynthesis
theories.claim: Light elements formed in the first minutes.

theories.name: Inflation
theories.claim: The early universe expanded exponentially for a moment.
theories.evidence: Flatness and uniformity of the CMB (still being tested).

theories.name: Hawking radiation
theories.claim: Black holes emit thermal radiation.
theories.evidence: Theoretical; analogue experiments only so far.

theories.name: Spontaneous symmetry breaking
theories.claim: Laws can be symmetric while their ground states are not.

theories.name: Quantum electrodynamics
theories.claim: Light and matter interact by exchanging photons.
theories.evidence: Lamb shift; electron magnetic moment to 12 digits.

theories.name: Parity violation
theories.claim: The weak force distinguishes left from right.

theories.name: Solar neutrino problem resolved
theories.claim: Missing solar neutrinos had changed type.

theories.name: Continental shelves and ocean currents
theories.claim: Ocean winds and currents follow global patterns.

theories.name: Atmospheric circulation cells
theories.claim: Air circulates in large cells, driving trade winds.

theories.name: Jet stream
theories.claim: Fast, narrow winds flow high in the atmosphere.

theories.name: El Niño–Southern Oscillation
theories.claim: Pacific ocean and air pressure swing together.
theories.evidence: Linked sea temperatures to the Southern Oscillation.

theories.name: Tectonic hotspots
theories.claim: Island chains form over fixed mantle plumes.
